newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs higher on Telebras, Motta.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs higher on Telebras, Motta.

text.p: Brazil shares were 2.99 percent higher at noon, boosted by Telebras which jumped 4.11 percent following comments by Communications Minister Sergio Motta on the selloff of the telecommunications sector.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks rose 355 points to 12,264 points by 1200 local/1500 GMT.
Total market turnover was a moderate 291.9 million reais (US$270.2 million), with traders projecting a volume of over 800 million reais for the day.
Traders said Motta's comments reiterating the government's plans to privatize the entire Telebras system by mid-1998 contributed to boost market sentiment after four consecutive days of losses.
"The market opened trendless, but Motta's remarks fueled buying of Telebras," an analyst said.
Brokers said, however, they were unsure whether the market would keep climbing throughout of the session because of the upcoming options and futures index contracts expiries.
"The options game began and the market can move in any direction before the settlements," one said.
Telebras preferred traded at 152 reais, accounting for over 50 percent of trade.
Other telecom stocks posted significant gains. Telesp preferred was up 2.34 percent at 350 reais, while Telemig preferred jumped 5.41 percent at 195 reais.
Telerj preferred was up 1.47 percent at 172 reais.
Telesp, Telemig and Telerj are units of Telebras serving Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro states, respectively.
